questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The coldest places on Earth
How to keep your home warm in winter
Why people feel the cold differently
How reindeer survive in the Arctic
questions.why: Phil asks why people feel the cold so differently, and that's what they discuss.

questions.q: What do Phil and Becca agree about?
options: They'd both rather be too hot than too cold
They both enjoy very cold weather
They both want to visit Finland
They both wear T-shirts in winter
questions.why: Becca prefers being too hot to too cold, and Phil says 'Yes, me too.'

questions.q: According to Phil, what is perhaps the most obvious thing affecting how we feel the cold?
options: Our age
What we eat
How much we exercise
The clothes we wear
questions.why: He says it depends on genes, culture and birthplace, 'but perhaps the most obvious thing is the clothes'.

questions.q: What does Professor Gunhild Sætren say is the first thing to consider?
options: Where you were born
Whether you are a man or a woman
How tall you are
What material your clothes are made of
questions.why: She says first and foremost gender differs; males are often more tolerant than females.

questions.q: What other factor does Gunhild mention?
options: Whether you have warm boots and gloves
How much sleep you get each night
Whether you're used to dealing with cold
How often you drink hot drinks in winter
questions.why: She says it's 'what you're used to. Are you used to dealing with the cold?'

questions.q: Who does Dr Cara Ocobock study?
options: Scientists living in Antarctica
Mountain climbers on Everest
Children in Brazil
Reindeer herders in northern Finland
questions.why: She studies reindeer herders, comparing them with ordinary Finns from warmer parts of the country.

questions.q: Why does Cara answer 'yes and no' when asked if reindeer herders cope better?
options: The results so far don't give a clear answer
Because she hasn't started her research yet
Because the herders refused to take part
Because she thinks the question is silly
questions.why: She says the more data they collect, 'the more confusing the picture gets'.

questions.q: What has Cara noticed about the reindeer herders so far?
options: They wear fewer clothes than other Finns
They seem to handle the cold better and shiver less
They feel the cold more than other people
They get ill more often in winter
questions.why: She says subjectively they handle the cold far better and are far less likely to shiver.
